newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 22.

text.p: Decision on parliament building deferred: The Cabinet has delayed making a decision on the future of new $94 million parliamentary building till next week. Page 1.
Sink-or-swim lessons over for NZ First newcomers: The government says it has learnt to swim, but its opponents are predicting more sinking from the coalition this parliamentary session. Page 2.
Peters loses support in seat -- poll: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters would lose if he contested his Tauranga seat today, a poll commissioned by ACT NZ has found. Page 2.

Arrest of dairy officials 'massive over-reaction': The charges six top Dairy Board officials were facing in Britain alleged criminal fraud, which was "a little different" from failing to pay duty on butter imports, board chairman Sir Dryden Spring said on Monday. Page 2.

Consumers should benefit -- Shipley: The government would judge the success of the reforms of the energy sector on the gains that must be delivered to consumers, State Owned Enterprises Minister Jenny Shipley said. Page 2.

Airport sales not yet on state agenda: The Crown could take between $100 million and $200 million out of Auckland airport as a capital repayment, but was unlikely to sell its 51.6 percent stake soon, industry sources said on Monday. Page 2.
Fletcher hopes for oil success: Fletcher Challenge Energy could be set for take-off if its Brunei oil concession fulfils hopes. Page 13.
BNZ lifts forecast for shares: Bank of New Zealand Investment Management said on Monday that it had lifted its 12-month return forecast for the sharemarket to nine percent from five percent. Page 13.
NZ Post to try insurance sales: NZ Post is to run a trial of the sale of insurance services through its Post Shop retail network from May 5. Page 13.

Max forecasts market improvement in profits: Max Resources is forecasting a significant turnaround in earnings during the next three years, moving from a loss of $882,000 for the year to June 30 1997, to a profit of $3.8 million in 1999. Page 13.

Notes in demand: The first issue of WestpacTrust's medium-term notes has been over-subscribed. The $50 million of three-year bonds carrying an eight percent coupon were placed with domestic institutional investors. Page 13.
